_comment: Authored wording for the public wiki payload (tools/build_wiki_data.py).
Only words live here: every number, name, address, rate and hash is read
from the game's own files at build time. Slots in braces are filled in by
the builder; a slot the builder cannot fill leaves the sentence out rather
than guessing. organised by the section of sample each entry serves.

sourceNotes.locale: {entries} keys. Every fact in the sample with a locale key beside it, and the full text of every help page.
sourceNotes.helpStructure: {categories} categories, {entries} page entries, {unique} distinct page slugs. {parse}
sourceNotes.layout: {items} placed items, authored at game build {build}. Shows where the game's own shops place this furniture; it is not a statement of what a layout must contain.
sourceNotes.buildings: {count} buildings from the game's fixed map. Gives every supplier address its neighbourhood, size code, floor area and traffic index.

lenientParse: not strict JSON: trailing commas dropped before parsing

steam.label: Steam app / depot build
steam.caveat: This is Steam's depot build id. It is not the game build number that a save file carries, and the two must never be compared.

saveBuild.label: Save build number
saveBuild.where: read from a save file, which this payload is not built from
saveBuild.caveat: Three build numbers exist and only two are visible here: Steam's depot build id for the install, and the build each shipped layout was authored at. Neither is the number a save carries, so this stays null rather than borrowing one of them.

pierFlag: The bundled building table puts the piers in {hoods}. The help names them all as importers; the neighbourhood a pier belongs to is not settled by either file alone.

prices.detail: None of the {pages} help pages the sample reads carries a money figure, so the sample states no price for any fixture, product, recipe or business it describes. {elsewhere}

gaps.pricesElsewhereOne: Money figures do appear in en.json, on {count} help page this sample does not read.
gaps.pricesElsewhereMany: Money figures do appear in en.json, on {count} help pages this sample does not read.
gaps.pricesNowhereElse: No other help page in en.json carries a money figure either.

missingProducts.what: Primary products the sample cannot describe
missingProducts.detail: The Gift Shop page names {products} as primary, but the matching help pages are missing from this build, so those sample entries hold nulls instead of facts.

weeklyLimits.detail: help_wholesalers_weeklylimits_content says every importer and wholesaler caps each item per week and that the cap resets Monday 08:00, but never gives a number for any item.

ratedRate.what: Rated rate is a ceiling, not a measurement
ratedRate.detail: Every recipe page gives a 'Max Production Rate Per Hour'. The help states that ceiling and nothing more: it does not say what a line achieves in practice, nor what happens when an ingredient runs out mid-hour. Big Copilot's day model takes that hourly maximum times 24, which assumes an uninterrupted line at full utilisation; no measured output lies behind it, and help text cannot supply one.

sizeCodes.what: Customer capacity by size code is ambiguous
sizeCodes.detail: {page} lists the same size code under more than one building type: {rows}. A size code alone therefore does not fix a shop's door limit, and the bundled building table stores only the letter.

danglingLinks.what: Help links that point at no page
danglingLinks.detail: {count} links across {slugs} distinct targets name a page the help menu does not contain, the most often {top}. The renderer has to degrade those links to plain text, not throw.

sourceQuirks.what: Malformed markdown and inconsistent names in the source
sourceQuirks.detail: {oddBoldClause} Supplier names are spelled more than one way for the same address: {spelled}.

buildNumber.detail: Steam's depot build id for this install is {steam}. The shipped layouts counted for placement were authored at builds {layouts}. Both are install facts; the third number, the one a save carries, is not in this payload because no save was read - and neither install number stands in for it.

wholesaleNegative.what: A wholesale 'no' is an absence, not a rule
wholesaleNegative.detail: {productsClause} the wholesaler product list, so the wholesale flag is false. That is two help pages agreeing, not a game rule: the help may simply not mention it.

sampleCoverage.what: The sample is one business, the pages are all of them
sampleCoverage.detail: The pages array covers every help page in the menu. The sample keeps the Gift Shop worked example the wiki page is written around: its fixtures, products, recipes and suppliers. Every other business reads its facts from pages, not from this sample.

provenanceNotes.sourceDate: sourceDate is the newest file modification date among the game help and counted layouts, not the moment this payload was built. An unchanged install therefore rebuilds byte-identical output; the sample's SOURCES block repeats it as sourceDate, and keeps the older extracted key with the same value for shapes written against the mockup.
provenanceNotes.determinism: Built from the game files named in sources. No run timestamp is written, so an unchanged install builds byte-identical output.
provenanceNotes.privacy: Source paths are game-relative. No absolute path, user name or save data travels in this file.
provenanceNotes.unparsed: {count} statements in the help could not be read into a field; they remain in the page text verbatim and are listed per record in the catalogue the extractor writes.
provenanceNotes.requirements: BUSINESS.requirements reads the business page's own requirement list. Its wording is kept in raw: the help says these are needed for the business to function, but not that the list is the complete set of rules the game enforces.
